text: Vuhledar is a coal-mining town in southwest Donetsk Oblast with about 14,000 pre-war residents.
Vuhledar's Soviet-era apartment blocks stand on high ground above flat, open fields, about 2 km north of Pavlivka.

observations.subject: distance from Vuhledar to Pavlivka (Vuhledar to the north)

text: From the roofs of Vuhledar's apartment blocks, Ukrainian observers overlooked the T-0509 highway and threatened the Donetsk–Volnovakha railway, Russia's only rail link between Donbas and the south.
In late October 2022 the Pacific Fleet's 155th and 40th Naval Infantry Brigades attacked Pavlivka, just south of Vuhledar.
The Russian naval infantry took most of Pavlivka by mid-November 2022.

In four days of the Pavlivka attack in autumn 2022 the 155th Naval Infantry Brigade lost more than 300 men and half its equipment, according to its own men's public letter, which blamed their commanders.

observations.subject: 155th Brigade men killed, wounded and missing in four days

notes: OUTCOME; the letter's figure covers killed, wounded and missing (see timeline 6–7 Nov)

text: On 24 January 2023 Russia attacked again towards Vuhledar from Pavlivka and Mykilske, with the same naval infantry plus Eastern Military District motor-rifle and tank brigades.
The Ukrainian 72nd Mechanised Brigade and its supporting artillery had been in place at Vuhledar for months before the January 2023 offensive.

For three weeks from late January 2023 Russian columns drove down the same dirt roads into a prepared Ukrainian kill zone at Vuhledar: the roads were left clear, the shoulders were mined, ATGM teams waited in the tree lines, and artillery was cued by drones.
Ukrainian artillery at Vuhledar fired US RAAM mines onto corridors that Russian mine plows had just cleared.
Ukrainian drone footage of Russian columns piling up on mines at Vuhledar went viral; the worst day was the assault of 6 February 2023.
By mid-February 2023 the Russian offensive at Vuhledar had culminated, and from late February Russia attacked with infantry alone.
Russian attacks at Vuhledar in March 2023 gained nothing.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

text: Russia's Eastern Military District commander, Col. Gen. Rustam Muradov, was reported dismissed on 3 April 2023.
Ukraine held Vuhledar for another 18 months after the 2023 battle; the town fell on 1–2 October 2024 to an attack on its flanks, not on its front.
notes: Epilogue, outside the chapter window (to 31 Mar 2023); not flagged OUTCOME

text: Within the chapter window to 31 March 2023, Vuhledar stays Ukrainian and Russia never holds positions inside the town.
notes: OUTCOME; the line is uncited in the dossier; cited as background to the ISW end-of-March assessment cited in 0006

text: Russian gains at Vuhledar to 31 March 2023 were a few kilometres at most: Pavlivka, Mykilske and parts of the dacha areas south and southeast of the town.
The Russian MoD claimed Pavlivka on 14 November 2022, but it was contested until at least 23 November 2022.
Russia took Mykilske about 27 January 2023.
ISW assessed in early March 2023 that Russia had "failed to advance four kilometers from Mykilske and Pavlivka to Vuhledar" in three weeks.

In mid-March 2022 the Ukrainian 53rd Mechanised Brigade fell back from Volnovakha to Vuhledar.
On 21 June 2022 the Ukrainian 53rd Mechanised Brigade retook Pavlivka from the Russian 810th Naval Infantry Brigade and separatist elements.

The 72nd Mechanised Brigade laid the minefields on the main approaches to Vuhledar from Pavlivka.
Forbes names the Ukrainian 55th Artillery Brigade as co-defending Vuhledar.
Ukrainian SOF teams worked with the 72nd Mechanised Brigade behind the lines at Vuhledar.
The Ukrainian 35th Marine Brigade and 56th Brigade fought on the approaches to Vuhledar and took Verkhni Dachi by April 2023.
The Ukrainian 68th Jaeger Brigade and the Belarusian Kalinouski Regiment were also reported at Vuhledar; Kalinouski activist Eduard Lobau was killed nearby on 26 January 2023.
notes: Not independently confirmed in the dossier

text: Ukrainian reserves were moved to Vuhledar quickly in late January 2023; Russian milbloggers claimed some came from Bakhmut.
No published Ukrainian strength figure for Vuhledar in 2023 was found; in 2024 the 72nd Brigade's new commander described a 1:9 force ratio against the brigade, referring to the 2024 battle.

observations.note: Ukraine : Russia, 1 to 9 against the 72nd Brigade, 2024 battle

text: Ukrainian ATGMs at Vuhledar included the Javelin and Stugna-P.
Ukrainian artillery at Vuhledar included M777 and Caesar howitzers, and HIMARS.
Ukrainian T-64 tanks at Vuhledar were used from hides at stand-off range.
Ukrainian forces at Vuhledar used DJI Matrice and similar quadcopters for spotting, plus small drones dropping charges.
Ukrainian mines at Vuhledar were TM-62 anti-tank mines, laid by hand or by GMZ minelayer, and the US M718 RAAM artillery-delivered mine.
About 6,000 US M718 RAAM shells were delivered to Ukraine in late 2022.
Zaluzhnyi named artillery ammunition as the binding constraint at Vuhledar.
The 72nd Mechanised Brigade was not rotated out of Vuhledar from February 2022 to its withdrawal in October 2024.
Lt. Vladislav Bayak of the 72nd Brigade described the Ukrainian kill zone at Vuhledar: a drone video feed spots a Russian column of about 15 tanks and APCs.
In the Vuhledar kill zone the dirt road was left free of mines and the fields around it seeded, "to entice the Russians to advance while preventing tanks from turning around", according to Lt. Bayak.

cites.quote: to entice the Russians to advance while preventing tanks from turning around

text: In the Vuhledar kill zone Javelin and Stugna-P teams in the tree lines opened fire; panicking Russian drivers swerved onto the mined shoulders and the wrecks blocked the road, according to Lt. Bayak.
In the Vuhledar kill zone Ukrainian artillery then fired on the stalled Russian column and on crews climbing out, according to Lt. Bayak.
Once at Vuhledar, HIMARS was used against a stationary Russian column, according to Lt. Bayak.

One Ukrainian tank crew at Vuhledar stopped about three miles short of its ambush site, out of range of return fire, and shot at targets it could not see, with a drone pilot calling coordinates over the radio.

observations.subject: Ukrainian tank firing position short of the ambush site
observations.note: three miles converted to km (about 4.8 km)

text: Ukrainian mines at Vuhledar were of two kinds: deliberate TM-62 belts, and RAAM shells fired onto corridors Russian mine plows had just cleared.
A moderator of the pro-Russian forum Lost Armour said Ukrainian RAAM fire at Vuhledar was "filling up the cleared corridor" behind Russian mine plows.
The UK MoD assessed that Ukraine's successful use of RAAM was the reason behind the heavy Russian losses at Vuhledar, as relayed by Novaya Gazeta Europe.
According to the UK MoD, Ukrainian RAAM was sometimes fired over and behind advancing Russian units at Vuhledar, to trap them on withdrawal.
Kyiv Post called artillery-delivered mines at Vuhledar a tactical surprise and the first large-scale use of them in the war.
Typical Vuhledar footage shows one Russian vehicle detonating a mine and the next driving past without slowing, only to hit another.
A captured Russian marine said the mobilised men at Vuhledar could not identify minefields or react to them.
A Russian tank milblogger blamed rushed mine clearing for the Russian losses at Vuhledar.
"Day after day, Russian armored columns were halted and then crushed by accurate shell strikes adjusted by" drones or by observers on Vuhledar's tallest buildings, according to Kyiv Post.

cites.quote: Day after day, Russian armored columns were halted and then crushed by accurate shell strikes adjusted by

text: On 6 February 2023 the Russians at Vuhledar smoked their advance with exhaust-injected fuel, but vehicles bunched up so closely behind the smoke that Ukrainian artillery could hit them by firing at its head.
Ukrainian fire at Vuhledar also hit the Russian rear, cutting supply and withdrawal routes.

Moscow Calling argued that Russian tanks without vision upgrades and units without communications or situational awareness at Vuhledar could only move in "slender columns": "If the Russian Armed Forces try to disperse, they will shoot each other".

cites.quote: If the Russian Armed Forces try to disperse, they will shoot each other

text: The Moscow Times says Russian tanks at Vuhledar went single-file for lack of demining equipment.
Russian armoured assault groups at Vuhledar were one tank and 3–4 IFVs; they drove to within 100–150 m, dismounted and attacked from the front and both flanks.
ISW judged the "highly dysfunctional tactics" of Russian forces at Vuhledar to reflect poorly trained mobilised men more than poor command.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

text: After the armour was spent, Russian infantry at Vuhledar advanced in waves and dug in behind burned-out vehicles; a 72nd Brigade soldier said: "They'd come in groups of five. We'd kill four, one would stay and dig in".

cites.quote: They'd come in groups of five. We'd kill four, one would stay and dig in

notes: Time not given beyond 'after the armour was spent'; dated to the infantry phase

text: Russian TOS-1A thermobaric launchers, a military-district-level asset, were used throughout the Vuhledar battle, which ISW read as a sign of priority.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

text: RUSI later noted that the destruction of a naval infantry brigade in an armoured thrust at Vuhledar reinforced Russian caution about using tanks for breakthroughs.
ISW judged that the Vuhledar losses prevented sustained Russian mechanised assaults elsewhere in winter–spring 2023.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

counter: RAAM fired onto freshly cleared lanes
rationale: At Vuhledar Ukrainian artillery fired RAAM mines back into corridors Russian mine plows had just cleared, trapping the followers between old and new mines.
effect: re-mines breached lanes minutes after clearing

rationale: On 6 Feb 2023 Russian vehicles bunched so closely behind their exhaust smoke that Ukrainian artillery could hit them by firing at the head of the smoke.
effect: smoke concentrated the column into a predictable target

counter: mined shoulders with a clear road (kill zone)
measure: armoured column advance along dirt roads
rationale: Leaving roads clear and mining the shoulders drew columns in and stopped tanks turning around; ATGM fire made drivers swerve onto the mines and the wrecks blocked the road.
effect: column stalled and destroyed in place

text: Set piece "Pavlivka in the mud" (late October – mid-November 2022): two Russian marine brigades attacked Pavlivka across the Kashlahach in rain and mud, took it street by street and lost half their equipment in four days, ending with their men's public letter of protest.

observations.subject: marine brigades' equipment in four days

text: On 3 February 2023 two 155th Brigade tanks moved up to firing positions near Vuhledar; the lead T-80 hit a mine and burned, and Ukrainian SOF and the 72nd Brigade captured two crew.

"Black Monday" (6 February 2023): a daylong Russian assault at Vuhledar by about two battalions under exhaust smoke, led by a plow tank, drove into the minefields; artillery fired into the smoke, about 30 vehicles were left behind, and the Alga battalion was mauled.

In a video published by Ukrainian marines in early February 2023, artillerymen comment as one Russian column blows up near Vuhledar and a second follows "exactly the same route"; this is the signature shot of the battle.

cites.quote: The second one went exactly the same route

text: In the filmed engagement ISW counted at Vuhledar in early February 2023, 13 Russian tanks and 12 BMPs were lost.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

text: The RAAM corridor at Vuhledar: a Russian plow tank clears a lane, and minutes later 155 mm shells scatter magnetic mines back into it, trapping the followers between old and new mines.
At Vuhledar HIMARS guided rockets, normally used against depots, struck a stalled Russian column.
In a strike reported on 13 February 2023, HIMARS hit the headquarters of the Vostok battalion near Vuhledar.

"The Wanderer": in the grey pre-dawn a Ukrainian T-64 crew at Vuhledar said a prayer and drove out against a column of 16 Russian tanks and armoured vehicles, stopped about three miles short of the ambush site and fired on coordinates from a drone pilot as the column stalled on mines.
The Russian officer's notebook (1–5 March 2023) records one assault group's daily tallies at Vuhledar of 100, 116, 103 and 115 men sent and 16, 23, 15 and 3 back.

observations.subject: men sent over four days
observations.note: sum of the four daily figures

text: Russia decided to attack Pavlivka in late October 2022; at the time Khodakovsky called it "premature".
ISW judged that at Pavlivka in late 2022 Russia had "impaled an insufficient concentration of mobilized personnel" and would have done better to wait.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

cites.quote: impaled an insufficient concentration of mobilized personnel

text: The 155th Brigade blamed Muradov, Akhmedov and Gerasimov for the Pavlivka attack decision.
After the Pavlivka attack, Pavlivka was taken and the 155th Brigade gutted, and the same Russian command repeated the plan at Vuhledar in January 2023.
ISW first read the January 2023 Russian attack at Vuhledar as an information operation or spoiling attack to distract from Bakhmut.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

text: The UK MoD saw the January 2023 Russian attack at Vuhledar as a "concerted offensive assault" to open a new axis.
Kyiv Post's sources later said the aim of the January 2023 Russian attack at Vuhledar was to cut off the whole Ukrainian Donbas grouping and break through there rather than at Bakhmut.
The UK MoD suggested the Russian MoD wanted a success of its own at Vuhledar to rival Wagner.
A Kremlin-affiliated milblogger judged that the Russians at Vuhledar lost the initiative by the end of January 2023 "due to Ukrainian forces' rapid transfer of reserves".

cites.quote: due to Ukrainian forces' rapid transfer of reserves

text: Pushilin likewise blamed Ukrainian reserves "in large quantities" for the Russian failure at Vuhledar; which reserves came from where is not public.
Leaving the roads clear and mining the shoulders at Vuhledar, rather than blocking the roads, was a deliberate Ukrainian choice to draw Russian columns in.
Firing RAAM into freshly cleared lanes at Vuhledar broke with the Soviet practice of laying narrow mine belts just before an attack.
The repeated Russian choice to send columns down the same narrow approaches at Vuhledar drew fire from milbloggers, who wanted Muradov tried.
Some argued the Russian units at Vuhledar had no alternative to columns: no communications, no situational awareness, "blind, deaf tanks".
notes: The dossier says 'some argued'; 0039 attributes this argument to Moscow Calling via CNN

text: The Moscow Times attributed the Russian columns at Vuhledar to a lack of demining equipment, and ISW put the cause in training.
Ukrainian commanders at Vuhledar called in HIMARS against a stalled Russian column, though HIMARS was normally reserved for depots and barracks.
In late February 2023, after losing "so many machines", Russia attacked at Vuhledar only with infantry, at the cost the Russian officer's notebook records.
Ukraine's General Staff reported on 4–5 March 2023 that Shoigu ordered Muradov to take Vuhledar at any cost amid a dispute between them.
ISW judged in early March 2023 that a renewed Russian offensive at Vuhledar was impossible without new reserves.

claimants.name: Institute for the Study of War

text: Muradov's reported dismissal followed the "at any cost" order, on 3 April 2023.
The Khortytsia group says higher command authorised the Ukrainian withdrawal from Vuhledar in October 2024.
A 72nd Brigade soldier told Kyiv Post that "the order to withdraw was never given" from Vuhledar in 2024.

cites.quote: the order to withdraw was never given

text: Analyst Kuzan said rotating the 72nd Brigade out of Vuhledar was discussed in 2024 but no reserves existed.
The 72nd Brigade's new commander called Vuhledar untenable with the forces available in autumn 2024.
On 7 February 2023 Russian Defence Minister Shoigu said Russian forces were "successfully developing" an offensive near Vuhledar.
In a broadcast on 12 February 2023 Putin said "naval infantry is working as it should right now" and that the Pacific and Northern fleets were "heroically fighting".

cites.quote: naval infantry is working as it should right now

text: The Russian MoD stayed silent on the losses at Vuhledar.
Russian sources claimed breakthroughs and positions inside Vuhledar on 26–30 January 2023 that footage did not confirm.
Pushilin claimed a Russian foothold on the southern outskirts of Vuhledar.
Girkin said of Vuhledar: "Ukrainian artillery shoots exceptionally accurately... the Ukrainians shot the attackers like in a shooting gallery".

cites.quote: Ukrainian artillery shoots exceptionally accurately... the Ukrainians shot the attackers like in a shooting gallery

text: Girkin said of the Vuhledar assaults: "Only morons attack head-on in the same place".

cites.quote: Only morons attack head-on in the same place

text: Wagner's Grey Zone channel attacked Muradov personally over Vuhledar.
Rybar called for "systemic changes" after Vuhledar.
A Kremlin-affiliated milblogger admitted the Russian offensive at Vuhledar had culminated.
Moscow Calling said 31 armoured vehicles of the 155th Brigade were destroyed in one assault at Vuhledar.

observations.subject: 155th Brigade armoured vehicles in one assault

text: A survivor of the 155th Brigade said eight men were left of his company.

observations.subject: men left of a 155th Brigade company

text: One Russian soldier said "up to 500" were killed at Vuhledar.
Relatives estimated 250–300 casualties in the Alga battalion at Vuhledar.
The Russian 5th Brigade made a video appeal to Putin over its losses at Vuhledar.
The Moscow Times' MoD sources said Muradov was relieved for the Vuhledar failures; one called him someone who would "order soldiers to go to certain death".

cites.quote: order soldiers to go to certain death

text: No official Russian figure for Ukrainian losses at Vuhledar was found in an acceptable source; Wikipedia's infobox cites a pro-Kremlin outlet claiming 200 Ukrainian killed and wounded on 24–25 January 2023, which the dossier does not use.
notes: Source of the figure rejected by the dossier

text: RUSI places Vuhledar at the start of an "ill-prepared offensive using under-trained troops [that] was extremely costly for the Russians".

cites.quote: ill-prepared offensive using under-trained troops [that] was extremely costly for the Russians

text: Michael Kofman described the Russian approach at Vuhledar as "repeatedly attacking in small mechanized formations through minefields, across open terrain".
